title: Mann's Own Kin Defects: CM's Cousin Joins BJP
excerpt: Gyan Singh Mann, a key AAP strategist from CM Bhagwant Mann's village, crossed over to the BJP in Chandigarh on May 11.
body:
Punjab's political temperature shot up on Monday when Gyan Singh Mann — cousin of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and a veteran AAP campaign strategist — formally joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in Chandigarh. The defection, coming less than nine months before the February 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, lands as a pointed embarrassment for the ruling Aam Aadmi Party.

**Who switched — and why:**
Gyan Singh Mann hails from the CM's ancestral village of Satauj in Sangrur district and had been a key strategist for AAP since its inception in 2013, managing Bhagwant Mann's campaigns and serving as a critical link in the party's Punjab leadership. He stated that he had joined AAP with the intention of contributing to Punjab's welfare, but became disillusioned with the party's functioning, alleging it had deviated from its original ideology and the promises made to the people of Punjab. He made a point of separating the personal from the political, saying 'CM Mann is like my brother and I stand with him personally, but I am quitting AAP.'

**The broader AAP crisis:**
This comes at a particularly bad time for the Arvind Kejriwal-led party, which is already reeling after seven of its Rajya Sabha MPs left for the BJP last month. Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini and Punjab BJP President Sunil Jakhar, addressing a joint press conference, welcomed the newcomers and said they had originally joined AAP with hopes for change, but after seeing those dreams shattered, had decided to join the BJP family. In a veiled attack on Arvind Kejriwal, Gyan Singh alleged that Punjab was effectively being controlled by leaders sitting in Delhi rather than by representatives from the state.

**What to watch next:**
With less than a year remaining before crucial electoral battles, this development is expected to intensify the ongoing political rivalry between AAP and the BJP in Punjab.
nri_angle: For the large Punjabi-American community — many of whom have family ties to Sangrur and surrounding districts — this high-profile defection signals deepening instability inside the AAP government that directly shapes life and livelihoods back home.
author: Diaspora Desk
